input.quote: Any writing or work of authorship created by M&I in the course of performing the Services under this Agreement, even if paid for by Customer, shall be the property of M&I ("Developed Software").
input.rationale: Section 10.4 vests ownership of all custom work of authorship in M&I expressly "even if paid for by Customer", and Customer's only right in M&I-provided software and modifications under 17.2 is use "during the Term to process its data". So we neither own the deliverables we fund (preferred position) nor hold any perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense them (fallback position); the Article 23 escrow licence is contingent and also runs only through the end of the Term. That fails the fallback on a material term. Customer Data ownership in 17.1 is favourable and is untouched, and M&I's retention of its platform and generic know-how is acceptable. The redline flips ownership of Customer-funded Developed Software to us with an express licence-back of M&I background IP, and offers the perpetual licence as the fallback landing.

proposal.summary: Customer owns Developed Software it pays for; M&I retains and licenses back its pre-existing/generic IP
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept that work of authorship we pay for becomes M&I's property with only a Term-limited right of use under 17.2, so we have flipped ownership of Customer-funded Developed Software to us while confirming M&I keeps its pre-existing and generic tools, know-how and platform. If M&I prefers to retain title, we can instead take a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Developed Software we funded.

ops.oldText: Any writing or work of authorship created by M&I in the course of performing the Services under this Agreement, even if paid for by Customer, shall be the property of M&I ("Developed Software"). M&I may make such Developed Software available to any of its other customers; provided, however, if Customer has paid for such Developed Software and M&I offers, as part of M&I's standard price list, a separate service resulting exclusively from such Developed Software, M&I will refund, or credit, to Customer a portion of any amounts paid for such Developed Software on terms and conditions agreed to by the parties prior to commencement of work on the Developed Software.
ops.newText: Any writing or work of authorship created by M&I in the course of performing the Services under this Agreement shall be the property of M&I ("Developed Software"); provided, however, that any Developed Software paid for by Customer shall be the sole property of Customer, and M&I hereby assigns to Customer all right, title and interest in and to such Developed Software. M&I shall retain ownership of its pre-existing and generic software, tools, know-how and concepts, and hereby grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense any such M&I materials to the extent embedded in or necessary for Customer's use of Developed Software paid for by Customer. M&I may make Developed Software that is not paid for by Customer available to any of its other customers. Nothing in Section 17.2 shall limit Customer's rights under this Section 10.4.
